text:
sarah: Quick ask — can we get a short synthesis of the Parallax-10B quant experiments? Product wants a recommendation we can hand off to GTN (cost vs fidelity, routing guidance, any priming regressions). TL;DR and one-line actionable please.

mike: Short TL;DR: int4 saves ~35% token cost vs int8 with small accuracy drop on short prompts, but multi-turn/priming quality regressions are non-trivial. Recommend mixed route: int4 for single-turn/safety-first endpoints, int8 for long-context & high-precision features.

anjali: Key numbers from the smoke run (sampled small prompt set) — precision is task-dependent but here are medians: answer-f1 drop ~2.8 pts int8->int4 on Q&A; 1.6 pts on summarization. Latency (p99) int8=210ms, int4=180ms on A100-40GB pool. Token cost per 1k (our internal units): int8 ~= $0.95, int4 ~= $0.62.

kevin: For product routing, concretely: route by turn_count & context_length. Heuristic we used in pilot: 
```
if context_tokens > 1024 or turn_count >= 3: model_variant = parallax-10b-int8
else: model_variant = parallax-10b-int4
```
This keeps most burst traffic on cheaper int4 while preserving fidelity for longer flows.

lina: Noted priming regressions: when we prepend 2-3 long examples, hallucination rate climbs ~1.5x on int4 for certain retrieval-augmented prompts. We ran masked-priming and saw decreased slot-fill accuracy on forms. Product implications: onboarding GTN features that rely on stable priming (e.g., few-shot behavioral tweaks) should prefer int8.

eval-bot: Auto-report: 50 eval tasks, 10k total tokens sampled. Scorecard summary link: https://redwood.internal/evals/parallax-10b/brief (internal). Overall score delta (int8->int4) = -0.037 (normalized utility). Regression alerts flagged: 3/50 tasks.

mike: Unit-econ example for GTN to quote: blended routing (70% int4, 30% int8) => blended_cost = 0.7*0.62 + 0.3*0.95 = $0.731 per 1k tokens. If product needs <1% quality loss target, tighten to 50/50 => $0.785/1k.

anjali: Operational notes: int4 uses more aggressive KV cache packing (saves memory) but we observed slightly higher peak memory jitter — autoscaler thresholds should be +10% headroom for int4 hosts in the dedicated pool.

kevin: Rollout recommendation for GTN: canary to 5% traffic with routing rules above + monitoring checks: drift in recall, hallucination rate, latency tail. Auto-fallback: if regression_count > 2 in 1h, fall back 100% to int8.

sarah: One-line actionable for GTN: default to parallax-10b-int4 for short single-turn endpoints to save ~35% cost, but pin long-context / priming-sensitive features to parallax-10b-int8 and use the 70/30 routing pilot with automated fallback on regressions.

lina: I'll open a short product doc with examples of prompts that regressed and suggestions for guardrails.

mike: I'll add the routing flag and canary config to the ops repo today. 

sarah: Great — please drop links here when ready. Thanks everyone :raised_hands:
